Apple's upcoming lineup next month will include a brand-new "iPhone Ultra" foldable device, but the most popular models will undoubtedly be the iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max. Here are six rumoured new features for the iPhone 18 Pro.

Design changes: Smaller Dynamic Island, unified back design

The iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max are expected to retain the basic dimensions and design of this year's models. However, three notable new changes will give the design a fresh look:

  • Smaller Dynamic Island
  • Unified back appearance
  • New colour options

With the Face ID components moving beneath the display, the Dynamic Island will become smaller. This will result in the smallest display cutout in recent years.

The two-tone back design of the iPhone 17 Pro received mixed reviews. To address this, Apple plans to better blend the colours of the aluminium and glass sections for a unified visual effect.

Rumours about the iPhone 18 Pro's colours suggest Apple is testing several new options, but the flagship colour expected to replace Cosmic Orange will be a deep cherry/burgundy tone.

A20 Pro chip

Every year, iPhones come with a brand-new chip. The A20 Pro chip in the iPhone 18 Pro is expected to be a particularly significant leap forward.

The A20 Pro will be Apple's first chip built using a 2nm process and will use WMCM (Wafer-Level Multi-Chip Module) packaging technology.

These two technological breakthroughs should deliver more notable improvements over this year's A19 Pro, making the iPhone 18 Pro outstanding in performance, efficiency, and AI tasks.

Variable aperture lens, improved telephoto lens, and more

Camera improvements are always one of the key upgrades for new iPhones.

For the iPhone 18 Pro, we expect a variable aperture main lens, offering greater control over depth of field. As my colleague Ben explains:

There are also rumours that Apple will introduce a telephoto lens with a larger aperture this year, along with more camera app features aimed at professional users.

Longest battery life ever

The iPhone 17 Pro and Pro Max came with the largest iPhone batteries to date and were extremely well-received. It sounds like Apple will continue to meet user demands by further boosting battery life.

The iPhone 18 Pro Max's battery capacity is expected to increase by approximately 10% over the previous generation. Further battery life improvements will likely come from the following two changes:

  • 2nm process of the A20 Pro chip
  • C2 cellular modem

The A20 Pro's new 2nm process is expected to deliver greater energy efficiency, and switching from Qualcomm's 5G modem to Apple's in-house C2 modem should achieve the same effect.

Camera Control 2.0

Camera Control first debuted on the iPhone 16 as a dedicated camera button offering various touch gestures to control zoom, exposure, tone, and more. However, many users found these features too complex and unresponsive to use beyond a simple button.

According to reports, Apple will update Camera Control for the iPhone 18 lineup with a more streamlined feature set. The touch component will be removed, and other changes may be made to provide a more user-friendly overall experience.

C2 modem

After years of development, Apple has officially begun replacing Qualcomm's cellular modems with its in-house solutions. The C1 modem debuted in the iPhone 16e, followed by the C1X in the iPhone Air, and now the C2 modem is expected to be used in the iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max.

Apple's 5G cellular modem has proven to deliver excellent performance while being more efficient and extending battery life compared to Qualcomm's solution. The C2 modem is expected to build upon the strong base established by the C1 modem series when it debuts in the iPhone 18 Pro.

iPhone 18 Pro features summary

Based on all the rumours and leaks we've seen, the iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max appear to offer the improvements users expect: stronger performance, longer battery life, moderate design adjustments, and camera upgrades.

What new changes and features do you hope the iPhone 18 Pro will bring? Let us know in the comments section.
